Court Made The Following:
 Order
The grievance of the Petitioner is as to acquisition of the subject property without due process.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner heavily banks upon Article 300A of the Constitution as Sri.Hanumantha Rao Gaikwad vs State Of Karnataka on 2 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114774013/
2 interpreted by the Apex Court in K.T PLANTATION vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA, (2011) 9 SCC 1.
She also relies upon P. G. BELLIAPPA vs. THE COMMISSIONER, BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, 2019 (3) Kar.LJ 795 and argues that where a citizen's property is knocked away by the State without due process of law which necessarily includes payment of compensation or public purpose, the property should be restored in lieu thereof recompense has to be made.

sentences.text: She also adds that despite there being a mandamus in the earlier round of litigation, nothing much has yielded to the hands of her client there being inadequate consideration of the material produced by him when the consideration took place at the hands of Respondent-Assistant Commissioner.

2. Learned AGA appearing for the State & its officials and the learned Panel Counsel appearing for the Court Registry oppose the Petition contending that whether one holds title to the property or not, ordinarily cannot be a subject matter of adjudication at the hands of Writ Court; parties at loggerheads have to lead both oral & documentary evidence, to prove their version; all property is presumed to belong to the State unless the contra is proved by cogent evidence.
No material worth mentioning having been placed on record by the Petitioner, no relief can be granted in Writ Jurisdiction.
A ritualistic enquiry as has happened at the hands of the Asst. Commissioner would not augur well, to a Welfare State ordained by the Constitution.

b) Learned counsel for the Petitioner is more than justified in contending that in terms of direction issued in W.P.No.47624/2015 (LA-RES) by a Coordinate Bench of this Court on 07.11.2017 there ought to have been a due consideration of the claim of her client, at the hands of the authority.

She rightly draws attention of the Court to several documents including a copy of the registered Sale Deed dated 22.12.1940,
which obviously being more than 30 year old, enjoys presumptive value under Section 90 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1972.

There is only a frugal reference to this Sale Deed in the impugned order; no discussion avails as to why this deed should not be believed to the advantage of the Petitioner; no reasonable citizen would be satisfied with frugality of the kind.
A perusal of the impugned order does not prima facie show that the authority has adverted to all and whatever material loaded to the Board.
Non-consideration of the relevant material constitutes an error apparent on the face of the record, warranting indulgence of this Court.

Sri.Hanumantha Rao Gaikwad vs State Of Karnataka on 2 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114774013/
3 c) Learned AGA appearing for the author of the impugned order vehemently contends that in matters like this, the right thing to do would be to relegate the Petitioner to Civil Court, admittedly property not being in his possession.

entities.text: Sri.Hanumantha Rao Gaikwad vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This course of action cannot be readily agreed to, when citizen is complaining about the violation of his constitutional right guaranteed under Article 300A.
In matters like that, Civil Courts would be a poor solace to the aggrieved.
Learned AGA sought to rely upon certain documents and contentions on the basis of what has been pleaded in the Statement of Objections.

It hardly needs to be stated that when a challenge is laid to an order made by a statutory authority like the Asst. Commissioner, its validity has to be adjudged on the basis of reasons assigned in the body of the order itself and that reasons cannot be outsourced, de hors the order vide MOHINDER SINGH GILL v. CHIEF ELECTION COMMISSIONER, AIR 1978 SC 851 to be dictated.

entities.text: MOHINDER SINGH GILL v. CHIEF ELECTION COMMISSIONER, AIR 1978 SC 851
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, this Petition succeeds in part; a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned order; matter is remitted to the portals of 3rd Respondent for consideration afresh, all contentions having been kept open; the consideration shall be accomplished within an outer limit of six months, of course, after notice to all the stake holders including the Respondent Nos.4 & 5.
It is open to both the sides to produce before the Asst. Commissioner, all and whatsoever documents supportive of their versions, within four weeks.

Costs reluctantly made easy.
Sd/-
